newsitem.title: UK: UK housing market leapt in Jan, Inland Revenue says.
newsitem.headline: UK housing market leapt in Jan, Inland Revenue says.

text.p: Britain's Inland Revenue said on Monday the number of houses sold in January leapt to their highest monthly level in about seven years.
The number of property transactions totalled 132,000, or 123,000 on a seasonally adjusted basis, compared with 109,000 in December and 104,000 in January last year, it said.
Although the figures cover property transactions as a whole, about 90 percent of the sales relates to housing.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders welcomed the news but warned against reading too much into the figures. "Although it can be misleading to place too much emphasis on one month's figures, this most recent data does confirm that transaction activity is now in line with the firming in house prices already experienced," said CML director general Michael Coogan.

Britain's housing market has been suffering from a chronic shortage of properties to buy. In certain areas -- particularly London and the South East -- prices have squeezed through the roof as a result.
"This will produce a sound and sustainable housing market recovery without the risk of overheating," Coogan said.
